name: Jordan Sullivan Dietitian (The Fight Dietitian)
shortDescription: Combat-sport nutrition at seminar length — making weight without wrecking the performance you made it for.
longDescription: An Australian performance-nutrition practice that names the athletes it has worked with, several of them current or former UFC champions. {{longCountWords|cap}} of the {{scannedWords}} most recent uploads run over twenty minutes and the median is {{medianPhrase}}, which is unusual density: these are seminars rather than clips. The specialism is the hardest problem in the subject — cutting to a weight class and arriving able to fight — treated as a physiological process with named failure modes rather than as willpower. Around it sits more general work on losing weight without the crash-and-rebound pattern, and on what a practitioner in this field actually eats. It sits against the endurance-fuelling voice already here: same discipline, opposite end of the sport, and the constraints could not be more different.
notFor: Anyone not competing in a weight-class sport will find much of the specialism irrelevant, and some of it actively unwise to copy — cutting weight is a supervised process, not a diet. Everything is seminar-length.

categories.why: The weight-class end of the discipline, where the constraint is making a number on a scale and still performing — the opposite problem from fuelling a long effort, and the one with the worst folk practice around it.
categories.evidence: A 56-minute seminar on making weight without losing performance, naming the three failure modes that recur in fight camps; 36 minutes on losing weight without the crash-and-rebound cycle; 18 on what a practising fight dietitian eats.

entryVideo.title: Make Weight Without Killing Performance - Jordan Sullivan AKA The Fight Dietitian
entryVideo.whyThisOne: The specialism at full length, and the clearest demonstration that weight cutting is a physiological process with predictable failure points rather than a test of discipline.

caveats: This is a nutrition company's channel and the seminars are its shop window; the athlete list is the company's own and we have not verified it. Weight-cutting protocols are demonstrated for supervised athletes and should not be copied unsupervised.
